definition: An archaic Dutch legal and medical term for sexual intercourse, literally 'sleeping alongside'; used historically in Dutch civil and ecclesiastical law governing marriage and adultery.
notes: Found in 19th- and early 20th-century Dutch legal statutes and medical literature. Virtually absent from contemporary speech; survives in historical legal scholarship.

definition: A polite Dutch euphemism for sexual intercourse, literally 'intimate contact/relations'; the standard soft-register phrase used in journalism, healthcare, and education.
notes: Default neutral phrasing in Dutch public health campaigns and news reporting when clinical precision is unnecessary but vulgarity must be avoided.

definition: The primary and most widespread crude Dutch verb for sexual intercourse; functionally equivalent to English 'to fuck' in vulgarity, frequency, and range of use.
notes: The single most common crude sex verb in Dutch; used across all age groups. Unlike English 'fuck,' carries no particular aggression by default — it is simply the blunt everyday word.

definition: Crude Dutch slang for sexual intercourse, derived from the standard verb 'to sew/stitch'; the sexual metaphor references the repetitive in-out needle-and-thread motion.
notes: Shares the sewing-as-sex metaphor with several other European languages. Slightly softer in subjective feel than 'neuken' for some speakers, but broadly equivalent in vulgarity. Both passive and active constructions are used.

definition: A lighter Dutch slang term for sexual intercourse, derived from the verb 'to seesaw/bounce/flip'; implies casual or playful sex without aggression.
notes: Notably milder than 'neuken'; usable in semi-informal contexts. The seesawing/bouncing imagery captures the physical motion of sex while keeping the register relatively benign.

definition: Crude Dutch slang for forceful, vigorous sexual intercourse, taken from the standard verb 'to ram'; emphasizes hard, repeated thrusting and implies the active/penetrating role.
notes: Directly parallel to English 'to ram.' Strongly implies the insertive partner's aggressive thrusting rather than mutual activity. Common in pornographic narration and crude boasting.

definition: Crude Dutch slang for sexual intercourse from the standard verb 'to thump/knock/bang'; emphasizes the percussive, rhythmic physical impact of vigorous sex.
notes: Cognate in register with British 'to bonk' and American 'to bang.' Very common informal slang throughout the Netherlands. Less aggressive in connotation than 'beuken' or 'rammen.'

definition: Crude Dutch slang for hard, aggressive sexual intercourse, from the standard verb 'to batter/pound'; implies more violence or force than 'bonken' and strongly foregrounds the penetrating partner's dominance.
notes: 'Beuken' also means to physically beat or pound something; the sexual use retains a distinctly violent undertone that 'bonken' lacks. Often used in pornographic contexts and aggressive crude speech.

definition: Flemish crude slang for sexual intercourse, derived from 'paal' (pole/stake); the metaphor frames the penis as a vertical pole driven into a partner.
notes: Predominantly Belgian/Flemish Dutch; low recognition in the Netherlands. The pole-and-stake imagery is more visually explicit than 'neuken' in foregrounding the mechanics of penetration.

definition: Dutch slang for sexual intercourse using the standard verb 'to ride'; often used for the on-top partner but can apply generically to any penetrative sex.
notes: 'Op iemand rijden' (to ride someone) implies the cowgirl or reverse-cowgirl position, but 'rijden' alone is used generically. Milder than 'neuken'; can slip into semi-euphemistic territory.

definition: Dutch crude slang for sexual intercourse, from the verb 'to tap/tick/knock'; used especially in youth slang to mean having sex with someone, paralleling English 'to tap.'
notes: Peaked in Dutch youth and hip-hop influenced slang in the 2000s–2010s. Partially influenced by American slang 'tap that.' Recognition is higher among under-40 speakers.

definition: Crude Dutch slang for sexual intercourse from the standard verb 'to pump'; captures the rhythmic, mechanical pumping motion of penetrative sex.
notes: The pumping metaphor is mechanical and moderately clinical in imagery while remaining unambiguously crude in register. Widely used and recognized throughout the Netherlands and Belgium.

definition: Flemish crude slang for sexual intercourse, derived from 'kachel' (stove/heater); the metaphor may relate to heat generation and vigorous physical effort during sex.
notes: Predominantly Flemish; very low recognition in the Netherlands. The etymology linking 'stove' to sex is unclear — possibly refers to heat from effort, or dialectal semantic drift. Declining frequency.

definition: Dutch slang for succeeding in having sex with someone, a direct borrowing from English 'to score'; frames sexual intercourse as a competitive achievement obtained through pursuit.
notes: Used identically to English 'to score.' Implies the speaker (typically male) successfully pursued and obtained sex with a target. Low vulgarity — the conquest framing matters more than graphic description.

definition: A basic Dutch euphemism for sexual intercourse using the general-purpose verb 'to do'; used when speakers want to imply sex without naming the act explicitly.
notes: Used in constructions like 'het met iemand doen' (to do it with someone). Universally understood by all Dutch speakers. Meaning is context-dependent; alone it is fully ambiguous.

definition: The standard Dutch euphemistic phrase for sexual intercourse, literally 'to do it'; the definite article 'het' anchors the referent and makes the sexual implication conventional and widely understood.
notes: The most default family-safe way to refer to sex in Dutch. Marginally more unambiguously sexual than bare 'doen' because 'het' is a frozen referent understood by convention to mean sex. Used across all age groups and social registers when directness is inappropriate.

definition: A Dutch euphemism for having sex with someone, literally 'to lie with'; carries a slightly archaic and literary register echoing biblical idiom.
notes: Echoes the biblical Hebrew idiom (cf. Genesis); still used in Dutch journalism and literature. Declining in everyday informal speech but well understood. Carries no aggression — softly romantic or evasive.

definition: Crude Dutch slang for sexual intercourse, literally 'to ride (a person)'; more explicitly sexual and objectifying than 'rijden' because the prefixed 'be-' makes the human object direct and specific.
notes: 'Berijden' is the standard verb for riding horses; applied to a person it is immediately crude and dehumanizing. The on-top/mounting implication is stronger here than in bare 'rijden.' Often implies the active or dominant partner.

definition: Crude Dutch slang for sexual intercourse from the standard verb 'to bang/blast/pop'; emphasizes explosive, energetic, vigorous sex.
notes: 'Knallen' primarily means a loud bang or gunshot. Applied to sex it implies high-energy, vigorous intercourse. Also used in Dutch youth slang as a general intensifier ('we gaan knallen' = we're going hard). Widely recognized.

definition: Crude Dutch slang for aggressive sexual intercourse, borrowed from the standard verb 'to hit/strike'; used in crude boasting or aggressive youth speech about vigorous or forceful sex.
notes: 'Slaan' (to hit) as sex slang is not universal — meaning is context-dependent and requires surrounding cues. More common in certain youth dialect groups and informal male speech. The violence-as-sex metaphor parallels English 'to smash.'

definition: Crude Dutch slang for sexual intercourse from the standard verb 'to clap/slap/crack'; onomatopoeically references the sound of skin-on-skin contact during vigorous penetrative sex.
notes: The onomatopoeic dimension (bodies 'clapping' together) parallels English slang 'clap.' Recognition is higher among younger speakers influenced by American hip-hop slang where 'clap' has the same meaning.

definition: Regional Flemish crude slang for sexual intercourse; etymology disputed but possibly derived from 'ros' (horse/steed), implying vigorous riding motion.
notes: Predominantly Flemish; very low recognition in the Netherlands. The 'horse' etymology would parallel 'berijden' metaphorically. Some sources connect it to dialectal Flemish for vigorous physical effort more broadly. Declining frequency.

definition: Crude Dutch slang for sexual intercourse derived from the standard verb 'to stab/stick/insert'; foregrounds the penetrative act as the defining motion with an implicit piercing metaphor.
notes: 'Steken' also means to sting (bee sting) or to stab, so the sexual use carries a mild violence connotation. Emphasizes penetration as the core act rather than the broader sex event. Used in both Netherlands and Belgium.

definition: Rare Flemish crude slang for sexual intercourse, derived from 'sloffen' (to shuffle along in slippers); the sexual metaphor is obscure — possibly referencing the rhythmic shuffling motion or implying lazy, perfunctory sex.
notes: Very low recognition outside specific Flemish dialect areas. The slipper-shuffle imagery is unusual and the origin of the sexual usage is poorly documented. Attested in some Flemish slang dictionaries but appears to be hyperlocal or near-extinct.

definition: Dutch crude slang for sexual intercourse derived from 'hossen,' the vigorous linked-arm group bouncing dance common at Dutch carnival and stadium events; the metaphor references the rhythmic, grinding, up-and-down motion.
notes: 'Hossen' primarily names a specific Dutch party dance (participants link arms and bounce rhythmically together). The sexual slang use exploits that same vigorous rhythmic physicality. Recognition is skewed toward those familiar with Dutch carnival culture; less widely known outside the Netherlands.
